column1: # NORMAN SCHEDULE / BATCH / LOSS-SCALE SWEEP -- 20 arms
# WHAT WE ARE TRYING TO ACHIEVE OVERALL
# Predict a perturbation's effect where that perturbation was never measured. Here the form
# is COMPOSITION: train on SINGLE-gene perturbations, predict PAIRS where both genes were
# seen individually and the pair never was.
# WHAT THIS SWEEP ANSWERS
# The shipped default (NQ02: Q02 base, 150 ep, eta_min 3e-4, batch 2048, lr 1e-3) was tuned
# on rhj_fewshot and moved to norman_combo wholesale. Four questions, each phrased so both
# outcomes mean something:
#   A  SCHEDULE   epochs {120,150,180} x eta_min {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3} at batch 2048.
#      On rhj 180 epochs was FLAT (+0.0003) and floors above 3e-4 COST. Only 30-vs-150 has
#      ever been compared on norman, so the interior is unknown here.
#      Outcome: a win inside the grid means the rhj schedule does not transfer; a flat grid
#      means the axis is closed on norman too and the default stands.
#   B  SMALLER BATCH -> MORE STEPS. batch {256,512} x eta_min {3e-4,1e-3} at 150 ep.
#      ⚠️ THE MEASUREMENT THAT MOTIVATES THIS GRID: rhj_fewshot has 612,122 training cells
#      = 298 optimiser steps/epoch; norman_combo has 56,971 = 27. The SAME recipe therefore
#      traverses its cosine schedule in 4,050 updates on norman against 44,700 on rhj -- an
#      11x difference in the amount of optimisation, invisible in the config. batch 512
#      gives 16,650 steps, batch 256 gives 33,300.
#      Outcome: if B beats the best of A, the schedule axis was never the binding constraint
#      on norman and the default was under-optimising by STEP COUNT -- which would also mean
#      re-checking batch size on any future small corpus.
#   C  LARGER BATCH at LONGER TRAINING, step-matched. The other side of the same axis: does
#      the step count matter, or the batch size itself? batch 4096 at 1200 ep gives 15,600
#      steps, i.e. B's step budget reached with 16x the batch. batch 8192 is 6 steps/epoch --
#      nearly full-batch on this corpus -- and is included as the ENDPOINT, not a candidate.
#   D  LOSS-WEIGHT SCALE. The three Q02 weights (dcos 0.32977, delta_mag 0.0400866, latent
#      MSE 0.00198826) are SCALE-MATCHED to this corpus by scripts/norman/norman_loss_scale.py,
#      which gives ONE point, not an optimum. A global 0.5x / 2.0x multiplier tests whether
#      the match is at the right level.
# ⛔ NA04 IS THE CONTROL, and it is not a duplicate. It is byte-identical in configuration
#    to the published NQ02 -- same base, 150 ep, eta_min 3e-4, batch 2048, seed 42 -- and
#    differs ONLY in that validation now composes pairs with `decode_seq_mean`
#    (panel_compose, new) instead of `sum`. So NA04-vs-NQ02 isolates the SELECTION METRIC:
#    same trajectory, same seed, different epoch kept. If NA04 beats NQ02, the published
#    checkpoint was chosen by a metric that disagreed with the reported one.
# HOW TO READ THE RESULT -- anchors, additive / nonadditive pearson_delta
#   meanpert 0.4634 / 0.4016 . OCCAM NQ02 (published) 0.8169 / 0.7380
#   sum_of_singles 0.8824 / 0.7757  <- THE BAR . experimental 0.9165 / 0.8377
#   Competitors: TxPert 0.8580 / 0.7139 . CellFlow 0.7603 / 0.6921 . State 0.6947 / 0.5905
#   ⚠️ Read all four metrics. `mae` is an ERROR, and it already splits this field
#      differently from pearson_delta (F-comp4).
# COST  20 arms, ~113 GPU-h. Column 26 is batch_size (optional, default 2048).
